system_prompt_style.note: Docs mention 'Zed's system prompt' but not how it is built; no source available.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: The agent can search your codebase to find relevant context, but providing it explicitly improves response quality and reduces latency.
env_context_strategy.note: User @-mentions (files, directories, symbols, diffs) are opt-in context injection.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: Compaction summarizes earlier messages and replaces them in the model context with that summary, leaving more room for the next turn.
context_compaction.evidence_locator: docs Agent Panel: Token Usage and Compaction
context_compaction.note: Automatic at the configured threshold via agent.auto_compact; manual /compact is also available. Tool-output truncation is not documented.

observation_format.note: The docs cover image input from the user but not the format of tool observations.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: Tool calling needs to be individually supported by each model and model provider.
tool_call_format.note: Inferred from the provider-level tool-calling requirement and the 'No tools' label.

tool_count.note: Docs say built-in tools exist for search, edit and terminal but give no list or count.

edit_primitive.note: An edit tool exists but its format is undocumented.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: You can add external tools with MCP Servers.
tool_schema_source.evidence_locator: docs Agent Panel: Using Tools and Profiles
tool_schema_source.note: The source of built-in tool schemas is unknown.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: Use External Agents for ACP-integrated agents.
protocol_standardization.note: Other = ACP (Agent Client Protocol) for external agents; MCP servers for tools.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: interrupting it at its next step (usually between a tool call and a response)

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: By default, the Agent Panel uses Zed’s first-party agent.
multi_agent_topology.evidence_locator: docs Agent Panel: Creating New Threads
multi_agent_topology.note: Parallel threads are independent of each other, not a delegation topology.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: Use Tool Permissions to control whether permission-gated tool calls are allowed, denied, or confirmed.
human_in_loop.evidence_locator: docs Agent Panel: Using Tools and Profiles
human_in_loop.note: on_completion = accepting or rejecting change hunks in Review Changes. The default policy is not stated.

long_term_memory.note: Skills can be @-mentioned, but the mechanism behind them is undocumented.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: The Thread History holds all your threads across all projects, sorted chronologically, and you can restore them at any time.
state_persistence.evidence_locator: docs Agent Panel: Managing Multiple Threads

rollback.evidence_quote: allowing you to return your code base to the state it was in prior to that message.
rollback.note: Restore Checkpoint mechanism; the underlying storage is not stated.

cost_controls.note: Token usage is displayed; no budget is documented.

permission_model.evidence_quote: Use Tool Permissions to control whether permission-gated tool calls are allowed, denied, or confirmed.
permission_model.evidence_locator: docs Agent Panel: Using Tools and Profiles
permission_model.note: Rules allow, deny or confirm tool calls; the default policy is unknown. Could also be static_allowlist.

tracing.note: Threads can be exported as Markdown; tracing is not documented.

target_domain.evidence_quote: The Agent Panel is where you interact with AI agents that can read, write, and run code in your project.
target_domain.note: general_tool_use is based on MCP support.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: Use LLM Providers for Zed-hosted models, API access, subscriptions, gateways, and local models.

primary_artifact.note: Only product documentation was available; closest value chosen.

pinned_version.note: No repo or version was supplied.
